# The object-listing target — verification record

*This file records the blind scan pass over the 18 object pages of the 90.05
listing, PDF pp. 199 to 216 (M4-1 chunks A2 to A8). One section per page. It
records what a reader measured on the page scan, and what that measurement
changed.*

The target was `test/fixtures/90.05-object-listing.target`. It was
scaffolding: the golden stayed the oracle of record, and chunk B7 matched it
against the target byte for byte, then deleted the target and its generator
(`docs/design/m4-codegen.md` M4-8 as amended).

## The method

Each page goes to one reader whose only source is the page scan. The reader
does not open the manual conversion, the target, or any golden. A reader
counts the page's rows before transcribing, and records blanks as well as
values, because a sweep that counts only values misses a row.

The comparison against the target is plain code, never the reader.

*Amended 2026-08-10, chunk A7.* Each page now goes to **two** readers, not
one. Neither knows the other exists. Their two readings are compared to each
other first, and only the agreed reading is compared to the target. A single
reader can hold a wrong reading with confidence; two readers who never met
cannot hold the same wrong reading by accident. The pages read this way are
20, 22, 23, 24 and 25.

One method note, from chunk A3. The rule that deletes a scanline whose longest
horizontal ink run reaches 25 px removes the solid form rules only. The dashed
rules print 6 px dashes, which that statistic cannot tell from text. Two
readers found two discriminators that work: the dashed rules print ink in the
left and right margins, where no text prints, and they cover a far wider
fraction of the page than the widest line of text.

A disagreement took one of two routes:

- The target was wrong. The correction went into
  `tool/object_listing_target_source.dart` (deleted with the target) and
  this file records it.
- The conversion was wrong. It became an erratum candidate in
  `docs/HANDOVER.md`, which waited for Jack's authorization and blocked no
  other page.

All eighteen object pages are verified.

Pages 8, 9 and 10 are chunk A3. Their 162 content lines carry no content
correction between them. Pages 11, 12 and 13 are chunk A4, and their 165
content lines carry none either. Pages 14, 15 and 16 are chunk A5, and their
165 content lines carry none either.

The three chunk A4 pages also pass a check no per-page reader could run.
Their location ranges are contiguous: 00264 to 00352, then 00353 to 00440,
then 00441 to 00527. No line is lost between one page and the next.

The three chunk A5 pages pass the same check, and they extend it across a
chunk boundary. Their ranges run 00530 to 00616, then 00617 to 00703, then
00704 to 00771. The first of them follows 00527, the last location of chunk
A4's last page, with no gap in octal. Six pages therefore run unbroken from
00264 to 00771, which no one reader could see.

## Listing page 8 — PDF p. 199

**Content: confirmed, with no change.** All 52 content lines agree with the
transcription in all six fields. The comparison found zero disagreements.
This page prints 52 lines, not 55, because it also prints the column header.

**Geometry: confirmed.** The reader fitted this page's own grid: character
pitch 9.2718 px at origin x = 411.38, after a deskew of -0.34 degrees. It
found the M4-8 columns — LOC at 0, OCTAL at 7, CNTRL at 25, labels at 34, the
`+n` offset right-aligned ending at 42, mnemonics at 49, operands at 56.

**The column header: confirmed on ink, independently.** The reader measured
`LOC` at 1, `OCTAL` at 12, `CNTRL` at 25 and `SYMBOLIC` at 58. That is the
2026-08-09 correction of `docs/design/m4-codegen.md` M4-8, measured again by a
reader who could not see it.

**Blank lines: corrected, and this page is not like the others.** The page
head is followed by **three** blank lines, then the column header, then one
blank line, then content line 1. The transcription holds one blank line in
each of the two places. The reader anchored the head at row 274.46, the
column header at 334.90 and content line 1 at 365.32, on a line pitch of
15.1654 px. That gives 3.985 pitches from the head to the header, and 2.006
from the header to line 1.

**The blank count is corroborated.** Page 8 is the one page that breaks the
pattern, so a second reader measured its vertical layout alone. It was given
the scan and the question, and no access to the first reader's work. It
reports printed rows in slots 0, 4, and 6 through 57 unbroken, and empty slots
at 1, 2, 3 and 5. It fitted the pitch at 15.1665 px on the run of 52
consecutive rows, with a maximum residual of 0.428 px, and no row deviates
from its integer slot by more than 0.043 slots. It swept each empty slot at
six ink thresholds and found exactly zero ink in the listing columns. Its
deskew angle, -0.34 degrees, is the first reader's to the hundredth of a
degree.

**The page head: confirmed.** The head agrees with the target byte for byte,
including the spacing that `docs/design/m1-front-end.md` M1-16 corrected on
2026-08-09. The head prints `PAGE` at columns 83 to 86 and its number at 89.
The body never prints past column 67.

**Doubtful glyphs, all resolved on ink.** Three, and each is a shape that this
print chain renders ambiguously. The `I` of `2,PI)1` carries full top and
bottom serifs and matches the `I` of `ID.` in the page head; the `1` two
columns right carries an upper-left flag and no top bar. The `*` of `*DATA` is
a solid mark at mid glyph height, where a period sits on the baseline and a
plus prints thin arms around a hollow centre. The `8` of `+8` closes two bowls
with rounded left sides, where the `B` of `BSS` prints a straight left stem.

**A caution this page raises: `O` and `0` print the same shape.** The reader
could not separate them by shape, and separated them by field instead —
letters in the mnemonic, the label and the head, digits in LOC, OCTAL, CNTRL,
the offset and the numeric operands. The measurement supports the split
weakly: 48 glyphs read as `O` average 8.89 px wide, and 1149 read as `0`
average 8.34 px. Page 9 reports the opposite, so this is a per-page property
of the print, not a fact about the chain.

**Two self-checks passed.** All 36 `OCT` lines print the octal word twice, in
the OCTAL field and as the operand, and the two agree character for character.
The LOC sequence is octally continuous through every `BSS` skip.

## Listing page 9 — PDF p. 200

**Content: confirmed, with no change.** All 55 content lines agree with the
transcription in all six fields. The comparison found zero disagreements.

**Geometry: confirmed.** Character pitch 9.2447 px at origin x = 439.98, after
a deskew of +0.25 degrees. The pitch comes from a least-squares fit over 2045
glyph centroids, with a residual RMS of 0.42 px. The M4-8 columns all hold.

**The `+n` offset is right-aligned. This page proves it.** It carries 42
offset lines, `+1` at columns 41 to 42 and `+10` to `+23` at 40 to 42. Not one
is left-aligned. M4-8 records page 200 as the only page that discriminates,
and a blind reader now measures the same result.

**Blank lines: corrected.** The page prints two blank lines between its head
and its first content line. The transcription holds one. The reader swept rows
197 to 211 and 220 to 231 at five thresholds and found no ink.

**Two attested M4-8 forms, confirmed on ink.** The 15-character name
INTERNAL.TOTALS prints alone on line 17, and line 18 prints `BSS 9` at the
normal columns with LOC, OCTAL, CNTRL and the label all blank. Lines 44 and 45
both print LOC 00165: line 44 prints `GN)000` alone, and line 45 prints
`START` with its instruction.

**Doubtful glyphs, all resolved on ink.** Six. Four are the first digit of LOC
on lines 52 to 55, faded on the left stroke, each read as `0` from a closed
top arc, a closed bottom arc and a full-height right stroke; a `C` on this
page prints an aperture between two curled terminals. One is the `I` of
`IOC)1`, which carries symmetric bars on a straight stem where the digit `1`
two columns right carries an angled flag. One is the two commas of
`CP)+14,0,CP)+15`, each of which strokes below the baseline where a period
does not.

**The redundancy check passed.** The 42 `OCT` lines print the twelve-digit
octal word twice. Both printings were read independently and agree on all 504
digits.

## Listing page 10 — PDF p. 201

**Content: confirmed, with no change.** All 55 content lines agree with the
transcription in all six fields. The comparison found zero disagreements.

**Geometry: confirmed.** Character pitch 9.321 px at origin x = 394.9, after a
deskew of -0.77 degrees, the largest tilt measured so far. Every token on all
55 lines lands on an integer column, with a residual RMS of 0.68 px over 1740
glyph left edges.

**Blank lines: corrected.** The page prints two blank lines between its head
and its first content line. The transcription holds one. The gap measures
46.0 px against a line pitch of 15.287 px, which is 3.01 slots.

**A form-rule caution for the pages still to verify.** On this page the dashed
form rules span x = 287 to 1479, so they cross the whole text zone and the
25 px run-length filter does not remove them. The reader found the rule rows
by their ink in the left and right margins, where no text prints. Rule
contamination caused three of this page's six doubtful readings.

**Three glyphs that high zoom read wrongly and the ink corrected.** The
mnemonic on line 17 reads `TKA` at high zoom, because its `R` prints a faint
top bar; it is `TRA`. The proof is the `R` of `CURRENT` on line 10, which is
certain from its doubled `R` and carries the identical defect row for row. The
CNTRL fields on lines 47 and 55 read as `1000C` at high zoom; both are `10001`
on the unrotated scan, where the right stroke is a straight stem broken on
three rows, and the page's 20 confirmed `C` glyphs never print that stem.

**One mark rejected as dirt.** Line 22 carries an ink speck one column past
its operand, at mid glyph height rather than on the baseline, and about a
quarter of a period's area. The operand is `BL)2,,15`, as on line 4.

**A form that a column-based comparator must handle.** Eight lines print the
six-character mnemonic `IOCTN*`. It ends at column 54 and leaves one blank
before the operand column, so a comparator that splits fields on two or more
blanks reads the mnemonic and the operand as one token. Ours did, and the
three lines it flagged were its own fault and not a disagreement.

**Three more line shapes.** Lines 27 and 35 print a location and a name only.
Line 36's 24-character name COMPARE.EMPLOYEE.NUMBERS runs from column 34
through the mnemonic column and into the operand column, and line 37 carries
that statement's mnemonic and operand alone. Line 52 prints `COM` with no
operand.

## Listing page 11 — PDF p. 202

**Content: confirmed, with no change.** All 55 content lines agree with the
transcription in all six fields. The comparison found zero disagreements.

**Geometry: confirmed.** Character advance 9.26708 px at origin x = 438.290,
after a deskew of 0.935 degrees, the largest tilt measured so far. The fit is
least squares over 2006 glyph centres spanning columns 0 to 98, with a residual
RMS of 0.432 px, and it holds a mean residual under 0.16 px in every column
decade. The reader anchored it independently on the page's one `OCT` line,
where the first location digit and the last operand digit are 67 advances
apart: 9.269 px by ink edges and 9.276 px by glyph centres.

**The M4-8 columns, found from ink alone.** The reader was given no column
positions. It measured the location at 0 to 4, the machine word at 7 to 21, the
control group at 25 to 29, the label from 34, the `+n` offset right-justified
with its last character at 42, the mnemonic from 49, and the operand from 56.
The page head prints `PAGE` at 83 and `11` at 89, which is the page 8
measurement of the head, and which binds PDF p. 202 to listing page 11.

**Blank lines: corrected.** The page prints two blank lines between its head
and its first content line. The transcription holds one. The reader swept both
slots at four thresholds, to 215, which is near paper white, and found zero
ink. Neither sweep window holds a form rule, so no row was dropped from either.

**The frame holds.** 55 content lines, none blank inside the body, and the last
one sits in slot 57.

**A hazard this page measures, for the pages still to verify.** The dashed form
rules sit at 30.387 px against a line pitch of 15.2145 px. That is 2.00 line
pitches, so a rule coincides with every second printed row. The 0.04 px per
interval difference walks the rule down the row as the page descends: it
crosses near the baseline at the top of the page and through the glyph bodies
lower down. Cell occupancy alone therefore fabricates glyphs on those rows.
This page's occupancy check flagged 39 inked cells with no character, and all
39 were the rule crossing one row's baseline.

**A print defect this page names.** The chain drops one vertical stroke of a
`0`, and the broken glyph mimics a `3`. The reader first read the machine word
at content row 48 as `0622` and corrected it to `0602`. Three lines of evidence
settled it: a `3` on this page carries a leftward waist where the doubtful
glyph carries a straight right stroke; the glyph correlates 0.886 against a
provably broken `0` on this page against 0.798 and 0.825 for the two certain
`3`s in its own row; and the mnemonic is `SLW`, which prints opcode `0602` on
two other rows. The same defect explains a `C`-shaped `0` in the location field
of six consecutive rows, and a `C`-shaped `D` in `END.OF.MASTERS`.

**Seven doubtful glyphs, all resolved on ink, and nothing unread.** Besides the
broken `0`, the reader separated four asterisks from `+` by their bottom row,
which stays 5 px wide where a `+` tapers to a point, and read the stop after
`ID` in the head as a period, which ends on the baseline where this page's
commas descend below it with a tail.

**Four self-checks passed.** The `OCT` line prints `747474747474` twice, in the
octal field and as the operand, and the two agree digit for digit. The location
sequence runs 00264 to 00352 with no skip. Every `+n` run is consecutive, and
each of the five labelled rows resets it to `+1`. Each of the 23 distinct
mnemonics maps to one opcode digit group, which is what confirmed the corrected
machine word.

## Listing page 12 — PDF p. 203

**Content: confirmed, with no change.** All 55 content lines agree with the
transcription in all six fields. The comparison found zero disagreements.

**Geometry: confirmed.** Character advance 9.31916 px at origin x = 398.838,
the centre of column 0, after a deskew of 0.855 degrees clockwise. The fit is
least squares over 2026 intensity-weighted ink centroids spanning columns 0 to
90, with a residual RMS of 0.585 px, which is 0.063 of a cell, and no whole
glyph further than 0.25 of a cell from its column. Line pitch 15.203 px, fitted
by a 55-tooth comb. The page's doubled-word line puts the predicted centre of
column 67 at 1023.22 and measures 1023.0.

**A method point this reader states, and the pages still to verify should
take.** Fit centroids, not left edges. A glyph's left edge depends on its
shape, because a `3` starts further right inside its cell than a `0` does, and
a left-edge fit carries that bias into the origin by more than a pixel.

**Blank lines: corrected.** The page prints two blank lines between its head
and its first content line. The transcription holds one. The reader swept the
print zone at five thresholds, to 220, and found zero ink on any non-rule row
in either slot. The one row in the gap that carries ink at the loosest
thresholds is the anti-aliased top edge of the first content line.

**The frame holds.** 55 content lines, none blank inside the body, and the last
one sits in slot 57. Every slot from line 1 to line 55 carries between 364 px
and 1447 px of ink, and the modelled slots above the head and below line 55
carry zero at all five thresholds.

**The form rules, and a warning about the run-length filter.** The rules run at
30.36 px, which is 1.997 line pitches, so a rule falls on every second line
slot and 150 image rows are rule rows. The filter that deletes a row whose
longest horizontal ink run reaches 25 px flags 28 rows here, and every one of
them is a solid rule: it misses every dashed rule on the page. The margin test
catches both. Because the rules cross the text, a content line has as few as 5
usable rows, so every cell was read from a crop.

**One glyph the ink cannot decide.** The operand of the `CAL` on line 7 reads
`?L)3`, and the first character is a double-loop form. This chain prints `B`
and `8` as the same shape, and the reader showed the classes do not separate:
cross-correlation puts the doubtful glyph at 0.820 to 0.874 against six certain
`8`s and 0.622 to 0.851 against three certain `B`s, and the certain `B`s
themselves score 0.755 to 0.893 against the certain `8`s. Left-edge
straightness and left-to-right ink balance fail the same way. The reader chose
`BL)3` on name structure: every other prefix on the page is all letters or a
single digit, so `8L` would be unique. The comparison then found the
transcription reads `BL)3` as well, and `BL)` is the block prefix the rest of
the listing uses. Two independent readings and the prefix's own attestation
agree, but the ink on this page does not choose, and a later reader should know
the alternative is `8L)3`.

*Jack's ruling, 2026-08-09.* He reviewed the glyph against the same comparison
plate, built independent arguments for both readings, and could not decide it
either. `BL)3` stands, and it stands on name structure and on the prefix's
attestation elsewhere in the listing, not on this page's ink. Record it as the
one character in the object listing that no reading has settled from the print.

*Annotated 2026-08-10, chunk A6.* It is no longer one character. The same
ambiguity appears at three more cells, on two further pages: `BL)3,2` on
listing page 17, whose reader leaned `8`, and `BL)2` twice on listing page 18,
whose reader leaned `B`. Jack ruled on 2026-08-10 that `BL)` stands at every
one of them, on the same grounds. **Treat `B` against `8` as a class this
print chain cannot separate at 150 dpi, not as a defect of one cell.** Four
sites are known and a later page may add more; each is decided by name
structure, and each is recorded in place rather than silently normalised.

**One mark judged a speck, and the transcription agrees.** A 4-pixel mark
prints right of the control group on the line at 00376. Every printed period on
this page is 11 to 15 pixels and reaches solid black; this one is faint, two
rows tall, and its centroid sits between cells at column 29.80. At five times
scale it reads convincingly as a period, and only at sixteen does it fail.
*Jack's ruling, 2026-08-09: not a period.*

**Three broken `0` glyphs**, each with the right stroke dropped, in a machine
word or a control group. The same defect page 11 named, and each sits in a
numeric field.

**An address that looks wrong and is not.** Line 11 prints location 00365 and
an address field of 00365, where every other `TXI` on the page addresses 00413.
The reader read the field three times from the raw bitmap and reported it as
printed. The arithmetic settles it: the operand is `SYS)245`, and 245 decimal
is 365 octal, so the address is correct and merely coincides with the line's
own location. The siblings address 00413 because they name `SYS)267`, and 267
decimal is 413 octal. Nothing here is anomalous.

**A label line that reserves no storage.** Line 14 prints location 00370 and
the label `GN)069` alone, and line 15 reprints 00370 with its machine word.
Page 9 records the same form at LOC 00165.

**Five self-checks passed.** Seven lines print their machine word twice and all
seven agree digit for digit. The location sequence runs 00353 to 00440 with no
break, and all seven octal carries are correct. Eleven distinct mnemonics map
to their opcode prefixes with no mismatch. Forty-seven lines carry a checkable
tag or decrement, with zero mismatches. Every address that names a label
resolves to that label's own location.

## Listing page 13 — PDF p. 204

**Content: confirmed, with no change.** All 55 content lines agree with the
transcription in all six fields. The comparison found zero disagreements.

**Geometry: confirmed.** Character advance 9.296 px at origin x = 421.97, which
is the centre of print column 0, after a deskew of 0.92 degrees. Re-running the
deskew search on the rotated page gives a residual of -0.04 degrees. The
advance comes from 2063 glyph centroids, fitted by the resultant of their unit
phasors, R = 0.9522, with a residual RMS of 0.478 px. An FFT of the body's
column-darkness profile peaks at 9.2985 px, and the page's doubled-word line
puts its last operand digit at column 67.07.

**This page proves the short baseline is a trap, with a number.** The
twelve-digit machine-word field alone gives 9.4545 px, which is 0.16 px per
column too large and more than ten cells of error by column 67. Chunk A3
recorded that its reader prompts named the wrong baseline and asked chunk A4 to
state it correctly. A reader that was told the correct baseline measured the
wrong one anyway, to see what it costs, and this is the cost.

**Blank lines: corrected.** The page prints two blank lines between its head
and its first content line. The transcription holds one. The reader counted ink
across print columns 0 to 88 at three thresholds over the whole band. The only
ink is one form rule, which crosses both margins where no text prints and spans
1.7 times the widest content line. Three single stray pixels at the loosest
threshold sit in three different rows and are scan grain.

**The frame holds.** 55 content lines, none blank inside the body, and the last
one sits in slot 57. Two proofs: every one of the 54 steps between line tops is
14 to 16 px, where a skipped slot would give 30.6 px, and one pitch fits all 55
tops with a maximum residual of 0.94 px.

**The form rules, measured further.** This page carries 32 rules at a mean
spacing of 30.548 px, which is 1.997 line pitches, and it refines what page 11
found: the rules alternate in weight, every third one solid and the other two
dashed. Both kinds fail the margin test the same way, so the margin test
removes both where a run-length filter removes only the solid ones.

**One mark judged not to be a character, and the transcription agrees.** A
faint mark prints right of the control group on the line at location 00465. The
reader left it out and recorded why: its centroid measures column 29.63, where
every certain period on the page lands within 0.07 of an integer column; it is
2 rows tall and 3 px wide where a certain period is 4 to 5 of each; it never
reaches solid black; and it sits above the digit baseline where this page's
commas descend to or below it. The nearest form rule is four rows away. The
transcription prints nothing there either, so two independent readings agree.
The report records the fallback, a period at column 30, for a later reader who
disagrees. *Jack's ruling, 2026-08-09: not a period.*

**Four doubtful glyphs, all resolved, and nothing unread.** The dropped-stroke
`0` that page 11 named appears here too, in a machine word, and the doubled-word
self-check resolved it. One operand was settled by counting cells before judging
spelling: `2)BONDENOMINATION,,1` fills exactly 20 cells, and a second `D` would
need 21.

**Four self-checks passed.** All three doubled words agree digit for digit. The
location sequence runs 00441 to 00527 with no skip, and each of its six octal
rollovers was crop-verified. The offsets run `+41` to `+94` unbroken. Every
operand that names an address reconciles against the octal printed on its own
line, including eleven `CP)` references that resolve against one base of 01674.

**A limit this page carries.** Every offset on it is three characters, so the
page cannot say whether the offset is left- or right-justified in its field.
Pages 9 and 21 settle that; this one is consistent with them and adds nothing.
Its one label likewise fixes one name's placement, not the label field's extent.

## Listing page 14 — PDF p. 205

**Content: confirmed, with no change.** All 55 content lines agree with the
transcription in all six fields. The comparison found zero disagreements.

**Geometry: confirmed.** Character advance 9.3291 px, line pitch 15.2232 px,
after a deskew of -0.412 degrees. The fit runs over the whole printed width,
print columns 1 to 68, and a second fit over 91 column-profile minima agrees
to 0.16 px across the page. The reader found the M4-8 columns.

**Blank lines: corrected.** The page prints two blank slots between its head
and its first content line. The transcription holds one.

**The frame holds.** 55 content lines, no empty slot inside the body, and the
last content line in slot 57.

**This page settles the offset justification again, on 52 lines.** The `+n`
offset is right-justified and ends at the last column of its field: `+1`
takes the last two cells and `+10` the last three, and the cell left of the
sign is blank on every one of the 52. A label, by contrast, is
left-justified and runs past its neighbour: `COMPUTE.PAY` reaches 11 columns
past the label column. Three lines print a label rather than an offset.

**The octal field prints two layouts inside one fixed span, and a later
reader must expect both.** Most lines group the twelve digits four, two, one,
five. Every `TXL` line and every `TXI` line groups them one, five, one, five.
One line prints a bare twelve-digit constant and leaves the last three
columns of the span blank. A comparison that assumes one layout mis-splits
ten of this page's 55 lines.

**Two marks judged specks**, each measured at peak ink 41 and 26 of 255 where
the floor for a printed cell is 200. Both are fragments of a form rule.

**A trap in the margin test, worth passing on.** The right-hand margin band
must start beyond the page head, which reaches further right than any body
line. A band that starts too far left puts the head's own page number inside
the supposed margin, and the test then deletes the head as a rule.

**Nine doubtful glyphs, all settled.** The page repeats the two defects
earlier pages named: `B` against `8`, settled on the left stem, which is flat
on a `B` and waisted on an `8`; and letter `O` against digit `0`, settled by
nearest-neighbour banks cut from this page, at the smallest margins on the
page. The current-location `*` prints as a solid blob at this reduction and
never resolves five strokes; it is settled on size, on mid-height position,
and on the arithmetic, because each of the three lines addresses its own
location plus `n`.

**Fifteen self-checks passed**, the location sequence and its octal carries
among them, and the reader reports one correction it made to its own report:
a first draft quoted an ink range it had swept over eleven slots and stated
as though it covered 55. It re-ran the full sweep and replaced the figure.

## Listing page 15 — PDF p. 206

**A method point that changed three readings on this page.** A form rule that
lies on a glyph's baseline pulls a template correlation to the wrong answer.
Three of the five near-ties here flipped for that reason alone. The fix:
measure the line's own rule profile in a column band where only the rule
prints, add that profile to each clean template, then correlate. Controls on
known glyphs confirm the correction does not push every result one way.

**A second method point, cheaper than the first.** A field that is constant
across the page is a free template at exact registration. Every location value
on this page begins with `0`, which gives 55 samples of that digit in the
column where the doubtful one sits. Look for such a field before building a
template from scattered instances.

**A third, on the defect the earlier pages named.** A dropped right stroke
opens a `0` for one or two image rows. A genuine `C` on this chain is open for
four. Aperture height settles the pair outright, where correlation settles it
by a thin margin.

**This page also prints an `EQU` line out of sequence**, between 00707 and
00710, and it breaks every other field assumption: no octal word, no control
group, and a label where the offset belongs.

**Eight doubtful glyphs, all settled**, and nothing on the page unread.

**Four sites judged specks.** The cleanest test on this page is position: with
a grid residual of 0.283 px, a mark 3.5 px from the nearest cell centre is
about twelve standard deviations from any character position.

## The eighteen pages run unbroken

**This check needs every page at once, so no page reader could run it.** With
all eighteen verified, the location column can be walked end to end. Four print
forms have to be modelled first, or each reads as a break: a `BSS N` prints one
line for N words, a wrapped label prints its word's location and pushes the
instruction that sizes it to the next line, an `EQU` prints an equated value out
of location order, and a `USE` or `ORG` switches location counters.

Walked that way, the three location counters hold 1021 words with no gap in any
of them:

| Counter | Runs | Words |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 00000 to 01620 | 913 |
| 1 | 01621 to 01771 | 105 |
| 2 | 01666 to 01670 | 3 |

**Two independent sums close on this.** Counter 1's 105 words are exactly the
five reservations the storage map prints — `RS)` 30, `TS)` 7, `BL)` 3, `PI)` 3
and `CP)` 62. Counter 0's 913 words are the 117 of the data region, 00000 to
00164, plus the 796 of the procedure text, 00165 to 01620, which chunk B1
derived from the location column alone. Counter 2 writes its three words over
the top of the `BL)` block, which is what its `ORG BL)1` line says it does.

page that stops early, at 48 content lines with its last in slot 51, which is
what the prediction expected of the final page: the listing ends, the frame does
not fail. Every page but one prints two blank slots after its head, and the one
that prints three is the one that also prints the column header.

**The prediction the chunk A2 pass wrote down was right on both of its named
tests.** It named listing page 19 and listing page 25 as the two pages whose
transcribed counts would test the frame. Page 19 was the transcription one line
short, and page 25 is the last page stopping early. Neither was an interior
blank line, which was the other explanation on offer, and no page of the
eighteen breaks the 57-slot frame.

## One flaw in chunk A3, recorded

The three reader prompts carried a wrong calibration hint. It told each reader
to fit the character pitch on "the location field against the far end of a
twelve-digit octal word", and called that about 59 columns. Those 59 columns
are the location field against the *operand* copy of the word, which only an
`OCT` line prints. The OCTAL field itself ends at column 21, which is 22
columns.

The page 10 reader caught it, said so, and fitted its own grid instead. Its
tokens land on integer columns with a residual RMS of 0.68 px over 1740 glyph
left edges. The pages 8 and 9 readers report pitches that agree with page 10's
to within 0.08 px, and the page 8 pitch is confirmed by a second reader. The
hint changed no reading. Chunk A4 must state the baseline correctly.

*Annotated 2026-08-09, chunk A4.* The A4 prompts stated it correctly, and the
page 13 reader then measured the wrong baseline on purpose to price the error.
The machine-word field alone gives 9.4545 px against that page's true 9.296 px,
which is more than ten cells of drift by column 67.

## One flaw in chunk A4, recorded

The pages 12 and 13 readers ran at the same time in one scratch directory, and
both wrote a working file under the same name. The page 13 reader's rotation of
its own scan overwrote the page 12 reader's rotation of its scan. The page 12
reader detected the change, moved its whole pipeline into a private
subdirectory, and re-derived every measurement from its own rotation of the
source. Page 11 ran alone and was never exposed.

**No reading is affected, and that is a measurement rather than an argument.**
Each reader's own reported origin and advance were applied afterwards to the
page it was asked to read. On all three pages the five columns of the location
field carry 47 to 67 times the ink of the blank column beside them, which a
grid fitted on another page's image could not do. The three readers also report
three different grids, so no one of them read another's file. The page 13
deliverable further matches the target byte for byte out to column 75, which a
wrong advance would break well before that.

Chunks A5 to A8 must give each reader its own directory. Concurrent readers
that share one are one filename collision away from a silent contamination,
and only a reader that happens to check its own working file will notice.

*Annotated 2026-08-10, chunk A5.* Each of the three readers got its own
directory before it started. Six readers ran at once, because chunk A6 ran
beside this one, and no file was written outside its owner's directory. The
fix holds and costs nothing.
